newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi police investigate Australian nurse's death.
newsitem.headline: Saudi police investigate Australian nurse's death.

text.p: Saudi Arabian police are investigating the death in suspicious circumstances of an Australian nurse at a hospital in Dhahran, a diplomat in the kingdom said on Sunday.
"It is understood that Saudi police are investigating the death," the diplomat said.

An Australian embassy official in the capital Riyadh said a consular official went to Dhahran in eastern Saudi Arabia on Saturday to "provide assistance and make inquiries" into the death on Friday of Yvonne Gilford, 56.
A foreign affairs spokesman in Sydney said earlier on Sunday Gilford died in suspicious circumstances at the King Fahd Military Hospital where she worked.
However a Sydney newspaper said Gilford had been murdered.
The Sun-Herald newspaper said Gilford was suffocated, stabbed and bashed with a hammer and was found dead in the early hours of Friday in her room at the hospital.
Two years ago, a nurse from the Philippines was stabbed to death at the base, the newspaper said.
It said Gilford, who had been in Saudi Arabia for six months, was last seen alive leaving a Christmas party.
It said it had been contacted by 14 other Australian nurses at the Saudi hospital who said they had barricaded themselves in their rooms for fear the murderer would return and wanted to go home.
Around 2,000 Australians work and live in Saudi Arabia, including several hundred in the medical profession.
